response.reason: NL1 is a descriptive/context statement about the overall purpose of the model and does not establish an independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes: (a) initial entry into an initial state owned by the braking device, (b) an endpoint from the initial state to the braking state on receiving a brake signal, (c) an endpoint from the braking state to the operational state when signal transmission fails, (d) an endpoint back to the initial state once signal feedback is sent. These three alternatives share source=initial state (the first two transition-group alternatives originate from the initial state: braking-signal-received goes to braking state, and... actually re-examine ordering). NL3 establishes an endpoint from the braking state to the brake caliper clamping state after entering the braking state. I model the transition group for NL2 as two separate groups: one from initial state (on brake signal) to braking state, and since "if signal transmission fails" is contingent upon being in braking state already (a failure of the signal that was sent to enter braking), the second transition source is braking state to operational state, and the third is from operational state (or braking state) back to initial state once feedback sent. I read the source discourse as: initial state -[brake signal]-> braking state; braking state -[signal transmission fails]-> operational state; then once signal feedback is sent, returns to initial state - ambiguous whether source is braking state or operational state. I treat this as continuing sequential narrative from operational state back to initial state, since it's the last-mentioned active state before completion (signal feedback presumably confirms successful transmission, which is the complement of failure, so it applies to the braking state's success branch instead). Given ambiguity, I extract endpoints preserving both readings as alternatives sharing source=braking state: fail->operational state, feedback-sent->initial state, forming a shared-source group from braking state with two alternatives (operational state on failure, initial state on feedback sent), consistent with "if...it proceeds to X. Once...it returns to Y" both describing outcomes stemming from the braking state's signal transmission attempt.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The closed FCSTM inventory establishes exactly BrakingState's outgoing edges as ClampingState (Entering_Clamping_State) and InitialState (Signal_Feedback_Sent, transition:line:16); no BrakingState->OperationalState edge exists, so the NL-required two-way branch sharing the BrakingState source does not exist as a realized alternative group. A competent alternative reading treats this gap as properly belonging to the separate endpoint-existence obligation (0021:r2:i0) rather than constituting an independent distinguishability defect, since disjointness/exclusivity as a semantic property logically requires both alternatives to be present before their guards/events can be compared; with only one alternative realized, there is nothing to which disjointness formally applies, so the alternative reading remains a live, competent doubt about whether this is truly a separate violation locus rather than a restatement of the missing-edge issue.

contract_extraction.reason: NL1 is a descriptive/context statement about the overall purpose of the model and does not establish an independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes: (a) initial entry into an initial state owned by the braking device, (b) an endpoint from the initial state to the braking state on receiving a brake signal, (c) an endpoint from the braking state to the operational state when signal transmission fails, (d) an endpoint back to the initial state once signal feedback is sent. These three alternatives share source=initial state (the first two transition-group alternatives originate from the initial state: braking-signal-received goes to braking state, and... actually re-examine ordering). NL3 establishes an endpoint from the braking state to the brake caliper clamping state after entering the braking state. I model the transition group for NL2 as two separate groups: one from initial state (on brake signal) to braking state, and since "if signal transmission fails" is contingent upon being in braking state already (a failure of the signal that was sent to enter braking), the second transition source is braking state to operational state, and the third is from operational state (or braking state) back to initial state once feedback sent. I read the source discourse as: initial state -[brake signal]-> braking state; braking state -[signal transmission fails]-> operational state; then once signal feedback is sent, returns to initial state - ambiguous whether source is braking state or operational state. I treat this as continuing sequential narrative from operational state back to initial state, since it's the last-mentioned active state before completion (signal feedback presumably confirms successful transmission, which is the complement of failure, so it applies to the braking state's success branch instead). Given ambiguity, I extract endpoints preserving both readings as alternatives sharing source=braking state: fail->operational state, feedback-sent->initial state, forming a shared-source group from braking state with two alternatives (operational state on failure, initial state on feedback sent), consistent with "if...it proceeds to X. Once...it returns to Y" both describing outcomes stemming from the braking state's signal transmission attempt.

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 is a descriptive/context statement about the overall purpose of the model and does not establish an independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes: (a) initial entry into an initial state owned by the braking device, (b) an endpoint from the initial state to the braking state on receiving a brake signal, (c) an endpoint from the braking state to the operational state when signal transmission fails, (d) an endpoint back to the initial state once signal feedback is sent. These three alternatives share source=initial state (the first two transition-group alternatives originate from the initial state: braking-signal-received goes to braking state, and... actually re-examine ordering). NL3 establishes an endpoint from the braking state to the brake caliper clamping state after entering the braking state. I model the transition group for NL2 as two separate groups: one from initial state (on brake signal) to braking state, and since "if signal transmission fails" is contingent upon being in braking state already (a failure of the signal that was sent to enter braking), the second transition source is braking state to operational state, and the third is from operational state (or braking state) back to initial state once feedback sent. I read the source discourse as: initial state -[brake signal]-> braking state; braking state -[signal transmission fails]-> operational state; then once signal feedback is sent, returns to initial state - ambiguous whether source is braking state or operational state. I treat this as continuing sequential narrative from operational state back to initial state, since it's the last-mentioned active state before completion (signal feedback presumably confirms successful transmission, which is the complement of failure, so it applies to the braking state's success branch instead). Given ambiguity, I extract endpoints preserving both readings as alternatives sharing source=braking state: fail->operational state, feedback-sent->initial state, forming a shared-source group from braking state with two alternatives (operational state on failure, initial state on feedback sent), consistent with "if...it proceeds to X. Once...it returns to Y" both describing outcomes stemming from the braking state's signal transmission attempt.
